sentiment.rationale: Micron delivered record fiscal Q4 revenue and EPS, and raised its forward guidance for FQ1-26 to record levels, with revenue expected at $12.5 billion and EPS at $3.75, up from the prior quarter's actuals. Management expressed strong confidence in continued growth, citing tight DRAM supply and robust AI-driven demand. The guidance raise is organic, driven by pricing, mix, and cost execution, not attributed to one-time items or FX.

summary.revenue: FQ4-25 revenue of $11.32 billion, up 22% sequentially and 46% year-over-year; FY-25 revenue of $37.38 billion, up 49% year-over-year.
summary.eps: FQ4-25 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.03, up 59% sequentially and 157% year-over-year; FY-25 non-GAAP EPS of $8.29, up 538% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: FQ1-26 guidance: revenue of $12.50 billion ± $300 million, non-GAAP gross margin of 51.5% ± 1.0%, non-GAAP EPS of $3.75 ± $0.15.
summary.margin: FQ4-25 non-GAAP gross margin of 45.7%, up 670 basis points sequentially; FY-25 non-GAAP gross margin of 40.9%, up 17 percentage points year-over-year.
key_risks: Potential new tariffs not included in guidance.
Supply constraints in D4 and LP4, with continued supply tightness expected.
Higher costs globally for new wafer capacity limiting supply growth.
Fiscal 2026 capex expected to be higher than fiscal 2025 levels, potentially impacting cash flow.
key_opportunities: AI-driven demand accelerating across data center, PC, and mobile.
HBM4 and HBM4E products with industry-leading performance and power efficiency.
Expansion of HBM customer base to six customers, with pricing agreements for 2026.
1γ DRAM node reaching mature yields in record time, enabling cost and performance advantages.
Data center business reaching record 56% of revenue with 52% gross margins.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly used phrases like 'outstanding finish,' 'positioned better than ever,' and 'strong momentum,' and provided record guidance, indicating high confidence in the forward outlook.

evidence.claim: FQ4-25 revenue was $11.32 billion, up 22% sequentially and 46% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Revenue of $11.32 billion versus $9.30 billion for the prior quarter and $7.75 billion for the same period last year

evidence.claim: FY-25 revenue was $37.38 billion, up 49% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Revenue of $37.38 billion versus $25.11 billion for the prior year

evidence.claim: FQ4-25 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.03, up 59% sequentially and 157% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share in fiscal Q4 was $3.03, with 59% sequential growth and a 157% increase versus the year-ago quarter.

evidence.claim: FY-25 non-GAAP EPS was $8.29, up 538% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: EPS reached $8.29, reflecting a 538% increase compared to the prior year.

evidence.claim: FQ1-26 guidance includes record revenue of $12.5 billion and EPS of $3.75.
evidence.quote: We expect revenue to be a record $12.5 billion, plus or minus $300 million, gross margin to be in the range of 51.5%, plus or minus 100 basis points, and operating expenses to be approximately $1.34 billion, plus or minus $20 million. Based on a share count of approximately 1.15 billion shares, we expect EPS to be a record $3.75 per share, plus or minus 15¢.

evidence.claim: FQ4-25 non-GAAP gross margin was 45.7%, up 670 basis points sequentially.
evidence.quote: The consolidated gross margin for fiscal Q4 was 45.7%, up 670 basis points sequentially.

evidence.claim: FY-25 non-GAAP gross margin was 40.9%, up 17 percentage points year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Gross margins expanded to 41%, a 17 percentage point improvement from fiscal 2024.

evidence.claim: Potential new tariffs are not included in guidance.
evidence.quote: Any impacts that may occur due to potential new tariffs are not included in our guidance.

evidence.claim: Supply constraints in D4 and LP4 are a risk.
evidence.quote: We continue to see supply constraints in D4 and LP4.

evidence.claim: Higher costs globally for new wafer capacity limit supply growth.
evidence.quote: On the supply side, we expect low supplier inventories, constrained node migration, as industry supports extended D4 and LP4 end-of-life, longer lead times and higher costs globally for new wafer capacity, all to limit the pace of supply growth for DRAM in 2026.

evidence.claim: Fiscal 2026 capex is expected to be higher than fiscal 2025.
evidence.quote: As we continue to make 1γ DRAM and HBM-related investments, we expect fiscal 2026 capex to be higher than fiscal 2025 levels.

evidence.claim: AI-driven demand is accelerating across data center, PC, and mobile.
evidence.quote: AI-driven demand is accelerating, and industry DRAM supply is tight.

evidence.claim: HBM4 and HBM4E products offer industry-leading performance and power efficiency.
evidence.quote: We believe Micron's HBM4 outperforms all competing HBM4 products, delivering industry-leading performance as well as best-in-class power efficiency.

evidence.claim: HBM customer base expanded to six customers.
evidence.quote: Our HBM customer base has expanded and now includes six customers.

evidence.claim: 1γ DRAM node reached mature yields in record time.
evidence.quote: We are proud to announce that our 1γ DRAM node reached mature yields in record time, 50% faster than in the prior generation.

evidence.claim: Data center business reached record 56% of revenue with 52% gross margins.
evidence.quote: In fiscal 2025, Micron's data center business reached a record 56% of total company revenue, with gross margins of 52%.
Micron had an outstanding finish to fiscal 2025, delivering fiscal Q4 revenue, gross margin and EPS all above the high end of our updated guidance ranges.

review_flags.reason: Score of 0.55 is based on a clear guidance raise and strong forward language, but the magnitude of the raise relative to prior guidance is not explicitly quantified in the document; reviewer may want to verify the prior guidance figures.
